summary: Moving a shape with the pointer while zoomed in no longer flattens it into blocks. Before this, one drag of a circle on a 24 point icon frame at 3200% turned it into visible squares that stayed until you changed the zoom.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Crisp zoom is on by default (next-crisp-zoom).

try.do: Open a blank canvas and choose Layer, New Frame, then the 24 size under Icons, then Add Frame.
Pick the Ellipse tool and drag a small circle inside the frame.
Press V for the pointer and look at the circle's edge: it should be a smooth curve.
Drag the circle one point to the right and let go.
try.shotNote: Photographed while the Mac was locked. The window is the real one, drawn and driven normally, with two known costs: colours can read dimmed, and a tutorial card does not draw at all because the login window is over it.

try.do: Look at the edge again without touching the zoom: it should be the same smooth curve.
Click empty canvas so nothing is picked, wait a few seconds, and look once more.
Nudge it again with the arrow keys and with the pointer a few more times, at different zooms.

evaluate: Does the shape ever flicker into blocks on the way through a drag, even for one frame?
Is the circle after the nudge exactly as smooth as the one you drew?
Does the sharpness come back fast enough that you never notice it being away?
Does dragging feel any slower than before?
rough: The sharp copy is still drawn about a tenth of a second after the drag ends, so on a very slow machine there may be a brief moment of the blown-up picture between letting go and it landing. That delay is deliberate and predates this fix.
The screen was locked for this run, so the pictures are real but their colours can read dimmed.
